newsitem.title: USA: Peco Energy interested in Maine Yankee buy - report.
newsitem.headline: Peco Energy interested in Maine Yankee buy - report.

text.p: Peco Energy Co is discussing a purchase of the Maine Yankee nuclear plant, but would expect to get the troubled facility at a low price, according to a newspaper report Thursday.

"We have had discussions with the owners for the possible purchase of Maine Yankee," Peco spokesman Bill Jones told the Portland Press Herald. "If we were to purchase it...it would probably come at a low price."
Maine Yankee officials Wednesday confirmed they had begun discussions about selling the 910-megawatt facility in Wiscasset, but refused to identify the potential buyer.

Maine Yankee is 38 percent owned by Central Maine Power Co, 20 percent each by New England Electric System and Northeast Utilities, seven percent by Bangor Hydro, five percent by Maine Public Service Co. and 10 percent by other New England utilities.
Maine Yankee officials refused to estimate what price they ask for the 25-year-old facility. The owners have $150 million in outstanding debt, according to spokeswoman Maureen Brown.
Any sale would have to be approved by the Nuclear Regulatory Commission. If approved, it would be the first sale of nuclear plant in the U.S., according to NRC officials.

Maine Yankee is on the NRC's Watch List for troubled nuclear plants, after having had two years of expensive safety related problems. The plant has been off-line since Dec. 6 and is not expected to return to operation until midsummer.
Philadelphia-based Peco already owns four nuclear facilities. It has experience fixing ailing nuclear plants, according to industry observers.

Problems at its Peach Bottom plant cost the utility $250 million in repairs and replacement power and brought a $125 million NRC fine, but by 1995 NRC officials were commending Peco for the plant's improved performance. ((--Boston bureau, 617-367-4106))
